extracted.intended_audience: general readers, fans, and researchers interested in Tig Notaro and contemporary stand-up comedy
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia biography summarizing Tig Notaro's life, career, and comedic style, including genre labels, quoted commentary on her approach, notable performances, and cross‑media work (albums, specials, memoirs, TV, podcasts). Useful for analyzing her comedic techniques and public reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedic genres/labels
rubrics_metrics.description: Genres listed in the article: observational comedy, black comedy, deadpan, surreal humor, cringe comedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These genre labels describe the range of stylistic modes associated with Notaro's work; they can be used as categorical criteria when classifying or comparing her material to other comedians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shift to personal comedy (post-diagnosis)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Notaro said that since her cancer diagnosis, she has shifted not to darker comedy but rather to personal comedy. Previously she was more distant and observational, but now she reflects on her childhood and life.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations of her work should account for a move toward autobiographical, reflective material that mines personal experience (including illness and family) rather than purely observational jokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadpan delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: The lead describes Tig Notaro as known for her deadpan comedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess performances for low‑affect, understated delivery and timing; deadpan is a central delivery style that shapes audience perception of jokes and punchlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transforming vulnerability through showmanship
rubrics_metrics.description: Quoted New York Times description: “She showed the audience her scars and then, through the force of her showmanship, made you forget that they were there. It was a powerful, even inspiring, statement about survival and recovery, and yet, it had the larky feel of a dare.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A criterion for strong material: the ability to present personal trauma authentically while using performance craft to keep the audience engaged and to reframe vulnerability as comedic and empowering rather than solely tragic. Examples include her topless Town Hall set where she revealed scars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eclectic/no‑fixed‑persona approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Notaro quote: “I'm always going to do whatever I think is funniest. If something's dark, I'll do it. If it's a sock puppet... There's no preconceived idea of who I think I might be now.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate creative risk and variety: willingness to mix registers (dark, silly, absurd) and formats without adhering to a single comic persona is a hallmark of her approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative storytelling and monologue technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples in the article include a monologue performed on This American Life (about encounters with Taylor Dayne, followed by Dayne's surprise appearance) and other longform storytelling pieces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider story structure, timing, escalation, and payoff in monologues. Effective use of surprise and real‑time narrative beats (e.g., guest appearance as payoff) is a measurable aspect of success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk‑taking and authenticity as performance choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Documented choices such as performing topless at Town Hall to show scars, and openly discussing cancer and personal struggles in sets and recordings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how candid, transgressive, or boundary‑pushing choices function artistically: whether they deepen audience connection, deliver comedic value, and are integrated into an overarching performance ethic rather than gratuitous shock.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross‑media comedic expression
rubrics_metrics.description: Notaro's work spans stand‑up albums, HBO/Netflix/Amazon specials, a memoir (I'm Just a Person), documentaries (Knock Knock, It's Tig Notaro; Tig), TV series (One Mississippi), podcasts (Professor Blastoff, Don't Ask Tig), and film work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating a comedian's body of work, consider adaptability of material across media, narrative continuity between formats, and how different formats (audio, video, written) amplify or constrain comedic techniques.
